summary: The returned BST must contain one node for every list value, making linear construction time unavoidable. Inorder simulation counts once and advances the shared list cursor once per result node.

optimality.argument: Any valid result contains n tree nodes, one for each input-list value, so constructing it requires Omega(n) time. The current method makes one O(n) counting pass, then creates each tree node while advancing the list cursor exactly once, for O(n) total time. Balanced size splits bound auxiliary recursion depth by O(log n), excluding the returned nodes.

replacement_checks.evidence: Materializing a BST containing all n list values requires constructing n result nodes.
One pass counts list nodes, and the construction phase advances the cursor and creates a result node exactly n times.
The source-fidelity-verified examples cover a multi-node list and the empty-list boundary; black-box real-test execution verifies every existing ordinary check without inspecting its definition.
